New Zealands injured Rachin Ravindra makes his way to the batting cage during a training session at the Basin Reserve. File | Photo Credit: AFP
New Zealand will miss more than just Mitchell Santner’s left-arm spin when it takes on India in the two-Test series, with Rachin Ravindra admitting that the white-ball captain’s leadership and presence in the dressing room will be equally difficult to replace.
Santner was ruled out of the series after fracturing his right hand while batting in the fifth ODI against India. Central Districts all-rounder Dean Foxcroft has been drafted into the squad as his replacement.
“He is such a big part of our team. That’s probably where we will miss him the most. He is a leader in the environment and such a great dude to have around. Obviously, his skill set is unique and amazing at what he does,” Rachin said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
“Super happy for Foxy (Foxcroft) to come in as well. He has done that role and has been playing well for New Zealand A. Feel for Sat and obviously, we’ll see how he goes in the next few weeks.”
Rachin is looking forward to making his comeback to international cricket at his home ground, the Basin Reserve, after recovering from a dislocated shoulder. The all-rounder last played competitive cricket for Welsh Fire in August and has spent the past eight weeks undergoing rehabilitation.
“It’s great to be back. It’s been a while since I’ve played. Watching the guys play on TV, you get a little bit of FOMO (Fear of missing out). You want to be out there,” said Rachin, who has been batting in the nets over the last three to four weeks.
Having enjoyed a prolonged break after a busy year, he hopes to return mentally refreshed for the red-ball challenge. “Hopefully it’s a blessing in disguise. It’s tough playing a lot of cricket, but it’s sometimes tough not playing enough either. Hopefully, I’ll be rested and mentally fresh,” he said
